metadata.titulo: The Song of Solomon (Song of Songs / Shir HaShirim)

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 1: Canto de Amor Místico y Comunión Espiritual
capitulos.textoOriginal: שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים אֲשֶׁר לִשְׁלֹמֹה: יִשָּׁקֵנִי מִנְּשִׁיקוֹת פִּיהוּ, כִּי-טוֹבִים דֹּדֶיךָ מִיָּיִן. לְרֵיחַ שְׁמָנֶיךָ טוֹבִים, שֶׁמֶן תּוּרַק שְׁמֶךָ--עַל-כֵּן, עֲלָמוֹת אֲהֵבוּךָ. מָשְׁכֵנִי, אַחֲרֶיךָ נָּרוּצָה; הֱבִיאַנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ חֲדָרָיו, נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בָּךְ--נַזְכִּירָה דֹדֶיךָ מִיַּיִן, מֵישָׁרִים אֲהֵבוּךָ.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Shīr ha-Shīrīm 'asher li-Shlōmōh: Yishāqēnī min-nəshīqōt pīhū, kī-ṭōvīm dōdekhā mi-yyāyin. Lə-rēaḥ shəmānēkhā ṭōvīm, shemen tūraq shəmekhā—'al-kēn 'ălāmōt 'ăhēvūkhā. Moshkhēnī, 'aḥărekhā nnārūṣāh; hĕvī'anī ham-melekh ḥădārāw...

traducciones.en:
1. Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for your love is better than wine.
2. Because of the savor of your good ointments your name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love you.
3. Draw me, we will run after you: the king has brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in you, we will remember your love more than wine: the upright love you.
4. I am dark, but lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
5. Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you feed your flock, where you make it rest at noon.

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 2: La Rosa de Sarón y el Lirio de los Valles
capitulos.textoOriginal: אֲנִי חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן, שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים. כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים, כֵּן רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת. כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר, כֵּן דּוֹדִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים... קוֹל דּוֹדִי, הִנֵּה-זֶה בָּא--מְדַלֵּג, עַל-הֶהָרִים, מְקַפֵּץ, עַל-הַגְּבָעוֹת.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: 'Ănī ḥăvaṣṣelet ha-Shārōn, shōshannat hā-‘ămāqīm. Kə-shōshannāh bēn ha-ḥōḥīm, kēn ra‘yātī bēn hab-bānōt. Qōl dōdī, hinnēh-zeh bā'—mədalleg ‘al-hehārīm, məqappēṣ ‘al-hag-gəvā‘ōt...

traducciones.en:
1. I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
2. As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
3. As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
4. He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
5. The voice of my beloved! behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
6. My beloved spoke, and said to me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away. For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone; the flowers appear on the earth.

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 3: La Búsqueda Nocturna y el Cortejo Celestial
capitulos.textoOriginal: עַל-מִשְׁכָּבִי בַּלֵּילוֹת, בִּקַּשְׁתִּי אֵת שֶׁאָהֲבָה נַפְשִׁי--בִּקַּשְׁתִּיו, וְלֹא מְצָאתִיו. אָקוּמָה נָּא וַאֲסוֹבְבָה בָעִיר, בַּשְּׁוָקִים וּבָרְחֹבוֹת--אֲבַקְשָׁה, אֵת שֶׁאָהֲבָה נַפְשִׁי... מִי זֹאת עֹלָה מִן-הַמִּדְבָּר, כְּתִימֲרוֹת עָשָׁן--מְקֻטֶּרֶת מֹר וּלְבוֹנָה, מִכֹּל אַבְקַת רוֹכֵל.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: ‘Al-mishkāvī bal-lēlōt, biqqashtī 'ēt she-'āhăvāh nafshī—biqqashtīw wə-lō' məṣā'tīw... Mī zō't ‘ōlāh min-ham-midbār, kə-tīmărōt ‘āshān—məquṭṭeret mōr ū-ləvōnāh...

traducciones.en:
1. By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
2. I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
3. It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
4. Who is this that comes out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 4: La Belleza Inmaculada y el Huerto Cerrado
capitulos.textoOriginal: הִנָּךְ יָפָה רַעְיָתִי, הִנָּךְ יָפָה--עֵינַיִךְ יוֹנִים, מִבַּעַד לְצַמָּתֵךְ... כֻּלָּךְ יָפָה רַעְיָתִי, וּמוּם אֵין בָּךְ. גַּן נָעוּל, אֲחֹתִי כַלָּה; גַּל נָעוּל, מַעְיָן חָתוּם.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Hinnākh yāfāh ra‘yātī, hinnākh yāfāh—‘ēnayikh yōnīm... Kullākh yāfāh ra‘yātī, ū-mūm 'ēn bākh. Gan nā‘ūl, 'ăḥōtī khallāh; gal nā‘ūl, ma‘yān ḥātūm...

traducciones.en:
1. Behold, you are fair, my love; behold, you are fair; you have doves' eyes within your locks.
2. You are all fair, my love; there is no spot in you.
3. A garden enclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
4. Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard;
5. A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
6. Awake, O north wind; and come, you south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 5: La Presencia del Amado y el Cántico a su Perfección
capitulos.textoOriginal: בָּאתִי לְגַנִּי אֲחֹתִי כַלָּה, אָרִיתִי מוֹרִי עִם-בְּשָׂמִי... אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה, וְלִבִּי עֵר; קוֹל דּוֹדִי דוֹפֵק... דּוֹדִי צַח וְאָדוֹם, דָּגוּל מֵרְבָבָה... חִכּוֹ מַמְתַקִּים, וְכֻלּוֹ מַחֲמַדִּים; זֶה דוֹדִי וְזֶה רֵעִי, בְּנוֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָם.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Bā'tī lə-gannī 'ăḥōtī khallāh... 'Ănī yəshēnāh, wə-libbī ‘ēr; qōl dōdī dōfēq... Dōdī ṣaḥ wə-'ādōm, dāgūl mē-rəvāvāh... Ḥikkō mamtaqqīm, wə-khullō maḥămaddīm; zeh dōdī wə-zeh rē‘ī, bənōt Yərūshālāyim.

traducciones.en:
1. I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk.
2. I sleep, but my heart wakes: it is the voice of my beloved that knocks!
3. My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
4. His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
5. His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
6. His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 6: El Regreso al Huerto y la Majestad Celestial
capitulos.textoOriginal: אָנָה הָלַךְ דּוֹדֵךְ, הַיָּפָה בַּנָּשִׁים... דּוֹדִי יָרַד לְגַנּוֹ, לַעֲרֻגוֹת הַבֹּשֶׂם--לִרְעוֹת בַּגַּנִּים, וְלִלְקֹט שׁוֹשַׁנִּים. אֲנִי לְדוֹדִי וְדוֹדִי לִי, הָרֹעֶה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים. מִי-זֹאת הַנִּשְׁקָפָה, כְּמוֹ-שָׁחַר: יָפָה כַלְּבָנָה, בָּרָה כַּחַמָּה--אֲיֻמָּה, כַּנִּדְגָּלוֹת.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: 'Ānāh hālakh dōdēkh, hay-yāfāh ban-nāshīm... Dōdī yārad lə-gannō... 'Ănī lə-dōdī wə-dōdī lī, hā-rō‘eh bash-shōshannīm. Mī-zō't han-nishqāfāh, kəmō-shāḥar: yāfāh khal-ləvānāh, bārāh kha-ḥammāh—'ăyummāh kan-nidgālōt.

traducciones.en:
1. Where is your beloved gone, O you fairest among women? where is your beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with you.
2. My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
3. I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feeds among the lilies.
4. You are beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
5. Who is she that looks forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 7: La Danza de Mahanaim y la Comunión de Amor
capitulos.textoOriginal: שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי הַשּׁוּלַמִּית, שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי וְנֶחֱזֶה-בָּךְ; מַה-תֶּחֱזוּ בַּשּׁוּלַמִּית, כִּמְחֹלַת הַמַּחֲנָיִם. מַה-יָּפוּ פְעָמַיִךְ בַּנְּעָלִים, בַּת-נָדִיב... אֲנִי לְדוֹדִי, וְעָלַי תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ. לְכָה דוֹדִי נֵצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה, נָלִינָה בַּכְּפָרִים.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Shūvī shūvī hash-Shūlammīt... Mah-yāfū fə‘āmayikh ban-nə‘ālīm, bat-nādīv... 'Ănī lə-dōdī, wə-‘ālay təshūqātō. Ləkhāh dōdī nēṣē' has-sādeh, nālīnāh vak-kəfārīm.

traducciones.en:
1. Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon you. What will you see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
2. How beautiful are your feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of your thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
3. How fair and how pleasant are you, O love, for delights!
4. This your stature is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters of grapes.
5. I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.
6. Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages. Let us get up early to the vineyards; there will I give you my loves.

capitulos.libro: El Cantar de los Cantares de Salomón (Shir HaShirim)
capitulos.capitulo: Capítulo 8: El Sello sobre el Corazón: El Amor es Fuerte como la Muerte
capitulos.textoOriginal: שִׂימֵנִי כַחוֹתָם עַל-לִבֶּךָ, כַּחוֹתָם עַל-זְרוֹעֶךָ--כִּי-עַזָּה כַמָּוֶת אַהֲבָה, קָשָׁה כִשְׁאוֹל קִנְאָה: רְשָׁפֶיהָ--רִשְׁפֵּי, אֵשׁ שַׁלְהֶבֶתְיָה. מַיִם רַבִּים, לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת-הָאַהֲבָה, וּנְהָרוֹת, לֹא יִשְׁטְפוּהָ; אִם-יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת-כָּל-הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ, בָּאַהֲבָה--בּוֹז, יָבוּזוּ לוֹ.
capitulos.foneticaLiturgica: Sīmēnī kha-ḥōtām ‘al-libbekhā, ka-ḥōtām ‘al-zərō‘ekhā—kī-‘azzāh kha-māwet 'ahăvāh, qāshāh khish-'ōl qin'āh: rəshāfēhā—rishpē 'ēsh shalhevetyāh. Mayim rabbīm lō' yūkhəlū lə-khabbōt 'et-hā-'ahăvāh...

traducciones.en:
1. Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which has a most vehement flame.
2. Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
3. My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: you, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.
4. You that dwell in the gardens, the companions listen to your voice: cause me to hear it.
5. Make haste, my beloved, and be you like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.
